dedupe_keys.name: osha injury tracking application establishment and case detail data

description: OSHA collects work-related injury and illness data through its Injury Tracking Application from establishments that meet industry and employment-size criteria, and publishes them by establishment. Summary data from OSHA Form 300A have been collected since 2016, and since 2024 certain establishments also submit case details from Forms 300 and 301; case detail data are published from calendar year 2023, and the 2023 and 2024 case files were updated with Occupational Injury and Illness Classification System codes. The current files cover injuries and illnesses of 2025 submitted between 1 January and 15 March 2026, and historical files cover each year since 2016. Coverage is the United States, per establishment, with industry codes. Downloads are free, and as U.S. Government works the data are in the public domain. Caveats: only covered establishments report, small firms and some industries are exempt, and case details come only from larger establishments in designated industries. For simulation it provides establishment-level injury records by industry, including manufacturing and chemical plants, for workforce safety, consequence and resilience analyses of industrial operations. Related catalogue records include the MSHA mine data sets for mines and the U.S. Chemical Safety Board investigations.
